chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Parents in Kentucky; father's death in 1921; bringing his mother to New York
summary: His parents stayed in Kentucky when he left; his father died in 1921, and he later moved his mother and sister's family to New York.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: You haven't told me what happened with your parents. Where were they -- you were still a young man, you're mid-20's.
That starts back when you leave Kentucky going to New York. It's that point in 1917 -- 1919, when we went to New York and our parents were still in Kentucky, both parents.
When you say "we" you're referring to you and Buck?
Your sisters remained back in Kentucky.

everybody remained back in Kentucky. And in 1921 we used to come from New York to Indiana- polis to see the Speedway races. We would drive out to see the races and then come to Louisville -- no Indianapolis to see -- at that time my mother was in Indianapolis -- to see my parents, my mother and my sister and my niece. And I'm driving away from there one day, coming back to New York and I decided, I looked in the mirror and saw my mother standing holding my niece in her arms and my little sister standing along- side of her and my father had passed away in 1921 and I went over to bury him and left my mother and I figured that this time, a couple of years later had passed when I saw my mother and I left and I decided I better get her away from there because she's there by herself all the time. So I thought I'd have her come to New York. I worked in New York at $100 a week, I only made $100 a week now under contract with Nazarro. So I'm going to take that $100 a week and bring her to New York and have her live there instead

Yeah, but there weren't but two. My sister and her child -- my niece -- my youngest sister and her child. Her child is my niece. My oldest sister's child was my niece. My mother's youngest daughter was there with her and I was the one, the only one left in the family to be gone, so I was going so I took my mother to New York with her and her little niece.
